title: ARMED: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Medication Recommendation
abstract: arXiv:2610.16440v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Medication recommendation requires jointly considering diagnoses, comorbidities, longitudinal patient history, and treatment interactions. Although recent retrieval-augmented generation approaches using language models have shown promise for clinical recommendation, most existing systems rely on fixed retrieval pipelines that cannot adapt to diverse clinical retrieval scenarios and may introduce noisy or irrelevant evidence. We propose ARMED, an adaptive clinical RAG framework that dynamically expands retrieval according to retrieval sufficiency and current-admission relevance. ARMED first observes the initial retrieval outcome and selectively performs supplementary or fallback multi-query retrieval when additional evidence is needed. The framework also incorporates a relevance gate that activates only clinically relevant same-patient history and organizes retrieved evidence into structured query-level clinical evidence. translated_title: ARMED：自适应检索增强的药物推荐
translated_abstract: 药物推荐需要综合考虑诊断、合并症、患者纵向病史以及治疗之间的相互作用。尽管近期基于语言模型的检索增强生成方法在临床推荐方面展现出潜力，但大多数现有系统依赖固定的检索流程，无法适应多样化的临床检索场景，且可能引入噪声或不相关的证据。我们提出了ARMED，一个自适应的临床RAG框架，能够根据检索充分性和当前入院的相关性动态扩展检索。ARMED首先观察初始检索结果，并在需要更多证据时选择性地执行补充性或回退性的多查询检索。该框架还引入了一个相关性门控机制，仅激活临床上相关的同一患者病史，并将检索到的证据组织为结构化的查询级临床证据。在……上的实验（摘要内容不完整）
tldr: 提出ARMED框架，通过根据检索充分性和当前入院相关性动态扩展检索，并利用相关性门控筛选临床相关证据，从而实现更准确的自适应药物推荐。
en_tdlr: ARMED is an adaptive clinical RAG framework for medication recommendation that dynamically expands retrieval based on retrieval sufficiency and admission relevance, using a relevance gate to filter clinically relevant patient history evidence.
